The bottles you opened with your notes, the wines you discovered elsewhere, your shopping list and insights.

While your cellar is empty and no other device syncs with this one, **Load sample cellar** (on the Cellar screen or in **Settings**) fills it with examples to explore every screen. **Erase all data** in **Settings** removes them when you are ready to add your own bottles; it also erases the cellar on the devices that sync with this one.

Start typing the name: if the wine is already there, choose it and only enter how many bottles you add and where they go.
Only the **name** is required. The producer and the vintage help tell wines apart; leave the vintage empty for champagnes and blends without a year.
The style (red, white, sparkling…) is used for colors, serving temperature and food pairing. The appellation, region, country and grapes make search and pairing better.
The years when the wine is at its best. It is estimated from the style and the vintage until you move the slider; enter the years from the producer or a guide if you know them.

Take a photo of the label or choose one in the add form. Reading the label on the device itself is not available on Android yet; the photo is kept with the wine.
If an AI service is set up in Settings, the label photo is sent to it to fill in the name, producer, vintage, style, region, grapes and drinking window. Only that photo is sent, never your cellar.
The AI only replaces fields that are empty or that were filled automatically. Everything you typed yourself is kept.
The label photo is kept with the wine, resized and without location data. You can change or remove it when editing the wine.
Describe your storage so every bottle has a place.
One bottle per cell, in rows and columns. Choose **two bottles per cell** for racks deep enough to hold one behind the other.
Every other row is offset by half a bottle and holds one fewer, like metal or terracotta racks. Enter the number of bottles in the widest row.
Shelves holding a row of bottles, one to three deep. The dots under each bottle show which places are filled, front first.
Diamond bins or crates hold several bottles in a pile. Set how many bottles fit in each; tap a bin to see what is inside.
Rows are lettered from the top and cells numbered from the left: **B3** is the second row, third cell. When a cell holds several bottles, **B3-2** is the second one (behind, or in the pile).
Each bottle shows its vintage, and its name once you zoom in. Tap a bottle to see what it is and where. Tap a wine in the key under the rack to light up its bottles; tap it again to show all.
Pinch to zoom in and out, or double-tap a spot; double-tap again to see the whole rack. Drag to look around once zoomed in. **Bottle list** lists the bottles of the rack place by place.
Tap a bottle, then **Move**, then the new place (or press and hold a bottle). Tapping another bottle swaps them; a bin takes the bottle if it has room.
Turn on **Rows of different lengths** for a rack under a sloped ceiling or a staircase, and set the length of each row.
When each wine is at its best.
Each wine is **kept for later**, **ready**, **to drink soon** (last year of its window) or **past its peak**. The label and the symbol always say it, not only the color.
Tonight shows the bottles to drink soon first. Choose a dish to see the wines from your cellar that go with it, and why.
Each wine page suggests a serving temperature and, for young full-bodied reds, how long to decant.
Keep track of what you opened and what you thought.
Swipe a wine to the right, or use **Drink** on its page. The bottle leaves the cellar and its place in the rack becomes free. **Undo** appears for a few seconds.
Add a rating, a few words and the occasion, or open the full tasting note (appearance, nose, palate, finish, food). Everything is optional and can be edited later from the Journal.
Use **Given away, sold or broken** for a bottle that left the cellar without being drunk by you.
At friends’, in a restaurant or on a trip, tap **Remember a wine** in the Journal and take a photo of the bottle. Add where you were, a rating, notes and tags.
Tags group discoveries your way: gift ideas, for summer, to try again. Tap a tag to select it, or type a new one; tags you used before are suggested.
Turn on **To buy** to add the wine to your shopping list, with the price you saw. When you buy it, swipe it to the right (**Add to cellar**): it leaves the list once the bottles are added.
Discoveries are not counted as bottles in your cellar and do not appear in racks or Tonight.
Use your own AI service for label recognition.
In **Settings**, under AI label recognition, choose a provider. You need an account with it and an API key; the provider bills you directly for what you use, usually a fraction of a cent per label.
Open the provider’s page with the link below the key field, create a key and paste it. The key is encrypted with the Android Keystore on this device and sent only to that provider.
Tap **Check key and load models**: the app asks the provider which models your key can use and fills the model menu. Choose a model that reads images.

Choose **Ollama**, **vLLM** or **LM Studio** if one runs on your computer, then tap **Connect and load models**. For Ollama, only the models that read images are listed: install one with `ollama pull gemma3`. On a phone or tablet, enter the computer’s IP address on your network (for example `http://192.0.2.10:11434`), and make the server listen on the network: `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` for Ollama, `--host 0.0.0.0` for vLLM, “Serve on Local Network” in LM Studio.
Leave it empty to use the provider’s usual address. Change it only if the provider gives you another one, for example for its China region.

Keep a copy and move your cellar.

**Export a backup (JSON)** saves everything: wines, bottles, racks, tastings and discoveries. Import it on another device, including an iPhone or a Mac, to restore it; nothing already there is replaced.
**Export a spreadsheet (CSV)** opens in any spreadsheet app, one line per bottle with its place. A CSV with at least a **name** column can be imported, including from another app.
Label photos stay on the device and are not included in backups yet.
Your cellar is stored only on your devices. There is no account, no tracking and no advertising.
Sync between your devices and with the people you share a cellar with is encrypted from end to end: a relay or WebDAV folder that stores the changes can never read them.

Apart from sync, only two things can leave the device, and only if you set them up yourself: the label photo, sent to your AI service, and the search terms of a wine, sent to your web search service when you tap Search.
Encave is open source: anyone can check what the app does.

What travels between your devices, and how changes come together.

First you pair your devices, once (see **Your devices**). After that they exchange their changes by themselves: directly when they are on the same Wi-Fi, or through a storage you choose when they are apart. Your cellar is encrypted from end to end all the way.
At home, on the same Wi-Fi

Paired devices find each other on the local network and connect directly, without going through the internet. A moment after each change (a bottle opened, added or moved), they send it to each other, photos included, over an encrypted connection. Encave must be open on both.

Optional, in **Devices › Sync away from home**: a WebDAV folder (a NAS, Nextcloud, pCloud) or a relay you trust (iCloud is for Apple devices only). Each device leaves an encrypted copy of the cellar there and reads the others’ about once a minute while Encave is open. The storage only ever sees encrypted files.

Every bottle, wine, rack, tasting, discovery and saved search remembers when it last changed. Changes to different things on two devices are all kept. If the same thing was changed on both, the later change wins. A deletion stays deleted, except that a wine comes back if someone added a bottle of it meanwhile on another device, so nothing added is lost. If two bottles end up in the same place, the one moved there last keeps it; the other stays in the cellar without a place. Every device ends up with the same cellar, whatever the order of the syncs.

When you remove a device (lost or sold), the cellar’s key changes by itself and the remaining devices receive the new one in an encrypted message. The removed device keeps what it already had but cannot read anything new.

Your AI and web search keys, your WebDAV login, the studio look and other display settings, and the choice of storage away from home: devices that do not sync away from home yet take it up the next time they meet on the same Wi-Fi, but turning it off or changing it applies to one device only, so do the same on the others.
The same cellar on your phone, tablet, iPhone and Mac.

On the device that has your cellar, open **Settings › Devices › Add a device**: it shows a QR code and a 6-digit code. On the new device, choose **Join another device’s cellar** and scan the QR code, or type the code. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi.

Both devices then show the same 6 digits and ask if they match. Check them before answering **They match**: different codes mean another device is in between, so answer **No**. This is what keeps your cellar private, even on a shared network.

Devices sync by themselves when they are on the same Wi-Fi and Encave is open, a moment after each change. You can edit on each device while apart: changes merge when they meet again. If the same wine was edited on both, the later change wins.
Bottles already on the new device
When joining, choose **Combine** to put both cellars together, or **Replace** to keep only the other device’s cellar (for example after trying the sample cellar).

Swipe a device in the list, or open its menu, and choose **Remove**. It keeps what it already has but can no longer sync with your devices: each device proves it belongs to the cellar with its own key, and the removed one’s key is no longer accepted.

To sync when your devices are not on the same Wi-Fi, open **Devices › Sync away from home** and choose a **WebDAV folder** you already have, or enter the address of a relay: a small open-source service that only stores encrypted files. You can run your own (instructions in the link on that page) or use one run by someone you trust. Devices that do not sync away from home yet take it up the next time they meet on the same Wi-Fi; turning it off or changing it applies to this device only.

A NAS (Synology, QNAP), Nextcloud, pCloud and many other services offer WebDAV. Enter the folder’s address, for example https://…/remote.php/dav/files/username/Encave for Nextcloud or https://webdav.pcloud.com/Encave for pCloud, with a username and an app password if the service offers one. Encave creates the folder if needed and checks that it can write there. Only encrypted files are stored in it. The username and password stay on this device: the other devices receive only the address, and show **Sign in to this WebDAV folder** until you enter a login on them too.

On the same Wi-Fi, devices talk directly; no server is involved. Through a WebDAV folder or a relay, only encrypted files are stored there. Every exchange is encrypted from end to end. The 6-digit code only helps the devices find each other: the comparison is what protects you.
Cherry, violet, a touch of undergrowth
Bought or ordered en primeur. The bottles join the cellar when you mark them received.
Bottles on order are listed apart and are not suggested for tonight until they arrive.
Received bottles join the cellar without a place; move them to a rack from here.
This bottle is on order: mark it received first.

Bought bottles that have not arrived yet, or wines bought en primeur? Turn on **Not delivered yet** and, if you know it, the expected delivery date. They are listed under **On order** in the Cellar and are not counted or suggested until you swipe them to the right (or touch and hold) and choose **Received**. They then join the cellar without a place, ready to be put in a rack.
Your own groups, such as gift, birth year or for a friend. Filter the Cellar by tag.
Group wines your own way (gift, birth year, for a friend) in the **Tags** of a wine. The Cellar shows a chip for each tag after the styles: tap it to see only those wines. Search finds tags too.
Estimated from the style and the vintage: ready %1$d years after the harvest, then at its best for %2$d years. Adjust it if the producer or a guide says otherwise.
The years entered for this wine.
Under the gauge, each wine says where its window comes from: estimated from the style and the vintage, or entered by you. **Drink sooner** and **Keep longer** move its end by a year.
Less than one bottle a month
to open every bottle before the end of its drinking window.
Bottles without a drinking window are left out: %1$d
On the first of each month, if bottles should be drunk this year, have just become ready or are past their peak, and on the day bottles on order are expected. Worked out on this device.
Notifications are off for Encave. Turn them on in the system settings.

Turn on **Reminders** in Settings: on the first of each month, a notification tells you how many bottles to drink this year, which have just become ready and which are past their peak, and another comes on the day bottles on order are expected. It is worked out on this device.
Their bottles and tastings are deleted too. You can undo right after.
No free place in this rack for bottles without a place.
Bottles taken out of their places: %1$d

In the Cellar list, choose **Select wines** in the sort menu (or touch and hold a wine, then **Select**), tick the wines, then place them in a rack, take them out of their places or delete them. **Undo** puts everything back.
Tap each bottle you find in the rack.
Taken out, they stay in the cellar without a place. Gone, they leave the cellar (given away, drunk elsewhere, broken). You can undo right after.
Take them out of the rack
Every bottle is where it should be.

Choose **Check this rack**, tap each bottle you find, then **End check**. For the bottles not found, choose **Take them out of the rack** (they stay in the cellar without a place) or **Mark them as gone** (they leave the cellar). **Undo** puts everything back.
Every wine with its places and purchase value, for insurance or a move
A CSV from CellarTracker, Vivino or a spreadsheet, read on this device

**Inventory for printing (PDF)** lists every wine with its number of bottles, places and purchase value: for your insurer, a move, or your family. The values are what you paid; Encave does not estimate market prices.

Export your cellar as CSV from CellarTracker, a spreadsheet or another app, then choose **Import from another app**. Columns are recognized by their name in English or French (wine, producer, vintage, color, quantity, location, bin, price, drinking window…). A Vivino history becomes discoveries, with your ratings and notes. The file is read on this device.
Point the camera at the barcode on the bottle
Allow the camera to scan the barcode, or type the digits under it.

When adding bottles, tap the barcode button: the camera reads the bottle\'s barcode and keeps it with the wine. The next time you scan a bottle of that wine, **Already in your cellar** appears: tap **Use this wine** to add bottles without filling anything in. Barcodes are matched on this device only; Encave looks nothing up online.
On tablets and large screens, the button at the top of the Cellar shows it as a list or as a table that sorts by any column, with the selected wine beside it.
On tablets, drag a bottle to another place to move it, or onto another bottle of the same rack to swap them (in racks with one bottle per place).
Touch and hold the Encave icon to **Scan a bottle** or see **What to open tonight** right away. A delivery reminder opens the wine on order.
The bottle stays in its place but is no longer suggested for tonight.

On a bottle in a wine’s page, choose **Keep for an occasion…** and name it (a birthday, Christmas dinner). The bottle stays in its place, is no longer suggested in Tonight, and the Cellar shows a chip for the occasion to find its bottles. **Free this bottle** gives it back.
The search engine that looks up a wine on the web when you tap Search online.
The address of your SearXNG server, on your network or online.
Created on the service’s website. Encrypted with the Android Keystore on this device.
SearXNG must answer in JSON: add json under search: formats: in its settings.yml.
Optional. Looks up a wine on the web to complete its details or find its current price, with the search service you choose.

Only the search terms are sent, directly to this service, when you tap Search: the producer, name, appellation and vintage of the wine, and the bottle size for a price. You see them and can change them first. Your cellar, notes and prices are never sent.
How to set up web search
Finds this wine on the web with %1$s. You see the search terms before they are sent.
Only these words are sent, to %1$s, when you tap Search. Change them if you like. Nothing else about this wine or your cellar is sent.
No pages found. Try fewer words.
Enter the full server address, starting with https:// (http:// only for a server on your local network).
The search service refused the key. Check it in Settings.
This SearXNG server does not answer in JSON. Add json under search: formats: in its settings.yml, then restart it.
Too many searches for now, or the free allowance is used up. Try again later.

The search service could not be reached. Check the connection and the address.
Kept with the wine and used for the estimated value of your cellar in Insights. Web prices vary: check them on the sites.
The only price found in %1$s. Change it if you like.
The middle value of %1$d prices found in %2$s. Change it if you like.
No price in %1$s was found. Tap a price below to use it with its currency.
No prices in these results. Try other words, or open a result below.

What a bottle sells for today. Counted in the estimated value of your cellar in Insights.
Complete a wine’s details or find its price on the web, with the search service you choose.
Nothing is looked up online until you choose a service in **Settings › Web search**.

**Brave Search** and **Tavily** need an API key, created on their website; both offer a free monthly allowance. **SearXNG** is a search engine you can run yourself, for example on a NAS: enter its address, such as `http://nas.local:8080`. Its JSON format must be on: add `json` under `search: formats:` in its `settings.yml`. Tap **Test search** to check.

On a wine’s page, or while adding or editing a wine, tap **Search online**. The search terms are shown first and you can change them; nothing is sent until you tap **Search**. Each result shows its title, a snippet and the site, and opens in your browser.

On a wine’s page, **Find current price** searches for the wine, its bottle size and the word “price”. Every price found is listed with its site; prices for several bottles, delivery or another size are left out. The middle value in your currency is suggested: change it or tap another price, then **Save price**. Insights adds up these prices for the bottles in your cellar as the **estimated value today**.

Only the search terms, to the service you chose: by default the producer, the name, the appellation and the vintage, and for a price the bottle size and the word “price”. Your cellar, notes, prices and places are never sent. The key is encrypted with the Android Keystore on this device.
It appears first among the filters, one tap away.

Search or choose filters, then **Save this search…** in the sort menu. The search appears first among the filter chips; tap it to apply it again, or touch and hold it to delete it. Saved searches sync with your devices.
The back label, the receipt, the bottle in its rack. They sync with your devices, encrypted.
To find a picture on the internet, choose a search service in Settings › Web search. The label photo is always kept.
No pictures found. Try fewer words.
This picture could not be downloaded. Try another one.

Only the search terms are sent to %1$s. The thumbnails and the picture you choose are downloaded from the sites that host them, which see the request and your IP address. Pictures from shops are for your private use. The label photo is kept.

On a wine’s page, **Change picture** then **Search pictures** finds pictures of the bottle with the same service. The one you tap is downloaded from its site and shown for the wine; the label photo is always kept. The thumbnails and the picture come from the sites that host them, which see the request. Pictures from shops are for your private use.
The bottles to open now, the most urgent first.
How many bottles you have, and how many to drink soon.
Scan a label or type a name.
No bottle is at its best right now.

On the home screen, touch and hold an empty spot, then choose **Widgets** and Encave. **Tonight** lists the bottles to open now and where they are (touch one to open it); **Cellar** shows how many bottles you have, and how many to drink soon or ready. Widgets show a summary kept on this device.
